搖鈴作為搖動體鳴樂器，常見於恰恰與爵士音樂，例如馬拉卡斯；在千里達、多米尼克與法: As a shaken idiophone the rattle is common in cha-cha and jazz, for example the maracas; in Trinidad, Dominica and the French Antilles there is the chak-chak. Some scores mark only rattle, without specifying the form. It also appears in folk ritual dance and in ancient Egyptian funerary rites; in the shamanic ritual and dance of Native Americans the raven rattle can express a chief's status. A baby's toy rattle belongs to everyday use.
搖鈴具有清脆、明亮的音色特徵，帶有輕快而富有穿透力的質感。其音域集中在中高頻區域: The rattle has a clear, bright timbre, light and carrying. Its range is concentrated in the middle and upper frequencies, so that it cuts easily through an ensemble. Its resonance is distinctive: the beads or metal pieces inside strike one another and produce a sustained sound with a slight grain, and the timbre has a clean, slightly shushing texture.
搖鈴在古埃及葬禮儀式中具有重要地位，早期多為卵形陶製，象徵死後重生，並被視為神聖: The rattle had an important place in ancient Egyptian funerary ritual, and the early ones were mostly egg-shaped and made of pottery, symbolising rebirth after death; they were regarded as sacred objects and became the forerunner of the sistrum. In the Predynastic and Old Kingdom periods the rattle gradually acquired a handle, and its shape and material shifted to basketry, wood and stone. In Native American cultures the rattle is often used in shamanic ritual and dance, and its figures are thought to connect with the sacred things of the tribe; the raven rattle symbolises power and shows in dance a chief's status and hereditary right to use it.
搖鈴是一種透過搖動發聲的打擊樂器，在霍恩博斯特–薩克斯分類法中屬搖動自鳴樂器，編: A rattle is a percussion instrument that sounds when it is shaken; in the Hornbostel–Sachs classification it is a shaken idiophone, number 112.1. How it sounds depends not only on the material but on how the sounding parts are arranged to strike one another when it is shaken. Uses include ancient Egyptian funerary ritual, Native American shamanic ritual and dance, folk ritual dance, and babies' toys; rattles such as sleigh bells are also used in cha-cha and jazz.
搖鈴的材質依文化與用途而異。古埃及早期卵形搖鈴以陶製成，後期出現籃材、木材與石材: The material of a rattle varies with culture and use. The early egg-shaped Egyptian rattles were of pottery, and basketry, wood and stone appear later. There are also egg-shaped plastic rattles containing steel beads, which sound when shaken so that the parts strike one another. 相比於鼓類樂器的厚實低沉，搖鈴音色更輕盈；相比於鈴鼓的清亮，搖鈴更具層次感與複雜: Compared with the thick, deep sound of drums, the rattle is lighter; compared with the clear ring of a tambourine, it has more layers and complexity. Its sound differs with the filling: a rattle filled with rice grains or sand has a soft, warm timbre, while one filled with metal beads is sharper and brighter. In a rhythm section the rattle gives a light swing, especially suited to cha-cha and Latin styles.
